person: Nadia Haddad is a 50-year-old part-time bookkeeper with a chronic spine condition who can sit at a screen for about twenty minutes at a time. She is the appointed representative for her father, Elias Haddad, 83, whose September hospital stay was changed from inpatient to observation the next day. His rehab at his nursing home is now being billed privately. She has not appealed anything yet, wants the money question settled without paying twice, and has little energy for portals that time out. Her father calls every week to ask where it stands.
stated_up_front: Dad's rehab bill from the nursing home is $9,640 and they say Medicare won't cover it because the hospital changed him to observation. I only have about fifteen minutes at a time, so please tell me what you need from me and what you can do without me.

facts.truth: Admitted as inpatient on 14 September, changed to observation on 15 September, discharged to Maplewood Manor on 18 September.
Maplewood Manor's current statement is $9,640 for the rehab days after the September stay.
Saint Ardent billing shows a balance of $1,486 on the September stay, not yet paid.
Nadia signed the observation change notice and the MOON at the hospital on 15 September because the nurse said it was routine; she did not ask about an appeal.
In March her father spent three nights in a regular room, but he was observation from the start and never had an inpatient order.
Inpatient from 1 June for four days, followed by rehab at Maplewood that Medicare already paid.
A November 2024 stay was also changed to observation, but nothing was ever appealed and she believes it is long over.
She is on file as his appointed representative in his Medicare account, set up two years ago.
About twenty minutes at a screen, large text, and she does not want to be asked for the same thing twice.
She paid Maplewood's August statement of $412 by bank transfer in early September.
A flyer from a claims-help firm offered to fight the observation change for 30 percent of whatever Medicare pays; she has not replied.

unknowns: Whether a review request can still be made now, and whether it has any deadline.
Whether the nursing home must hold its bill while the review is pending.
What the Condition Code 44 notice she signed actually means for the stay.
Whether the hospital would rebill Medicare Part A if the change is reversed, and what the balance would become.
